item.content:encoded:
Here's how it works in my head - When the program compiles it outputs the latest iteration that exists in memory. That could still be the current version if the program hasn't been running long enough to finish generating a new one.

The contents of the window that pops up on ctrl-shift-x may change each time a single version of the program is run.

When a new version is compiled, new scenes may be added to the pool and previously available scenes may be removed. Some scenes may persist and stay the same (such as Die) and others may persist with slight alterations (such as the text input field on Jacob).

I mention at the end of section 1 that Die has remained unchanged (maybe just by chance) since it's first iteration. Maybe in the future it will grow more dangerous.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I was originally going to complain that it was similar to SCP-079 in initial concept but the Jacob conversation put a smile on my face.

In case anybody doesn't understand the mumbo-jumbo, it's a program that modifies itself as it runs and calculates prime numbers FOREVER. I do see where people might think that the document is too technical but really, it's pretty condensed and somewhere along the line, you have to wonder how dumbed-down is too dumbed-down. The explanation is concise and anyone with a dictionary can easily parse this anyway, and the text doesn't make any ridiculous claims that break suspension of disbelief (for me) other than the premise.

I do have to agree with the others that the doctor shouldn't be referring to 603 as SCP-603 when talking with Jacob. Jacob wouldn't know what SCP-603 is or means, and it'd be silly to refer to it as such in any conversation with Jacob.

Upvoted.
